summary: 丝绸在中国先是宫廷专用面料，后来进入日常生活，还充当支付手段与外贸商品。随着养蚕技术外传，生产扩至亚洲和欧洲，近现代的生产中心又发生转移。
logic: 从宫廷穿着到各阶层使用

paragraphs.brief: 4500多年前中国首次发现丝绸时，它专供皇帝、其亲密关系及其最高贵宾使用。
sentences: When silk was first discovered in China over 4,500 years ago, it was reserved exclusively for the use of the emperor, his close relations and the very highest of his dignitaries.
4500多年前中国首次发现丝绸时，它专供皇帝、其亲密关系及其最高贵宾使用。
Within the palace, the emperor is believed to have worn a robe of white silk; outside, he, his principal wife, and the heir to the throne wore yellow, the colour of the earth.
在皇宫内，皇帝据信穿着白丝袍；在外边，他，他的主要妻子和王位继承人，穿的是黄色的，是地球的颜色。

paragraphs.brief: 渐渐的丝绸被广泛使用，中国社会各阶层开始穿丝绸。
sentences: Gradually silk came into more general use, and the various classes of Chinese society began wearing tunics of silk.
渐渐的丝绸被广泛使用，中国社会各阶层开始穿丝绸。
As well as being used for clothing and decoration, silk was quite quickly put to industrial use, and rapidly became one of the principal elements of the Chinese economy.
丝绸除了用于服装和装饰外，还很快被投入工业使用，并迅速成为中国经济的主要组成部分之一。
It was used in the production of musical instruments, as string for fishing, and even as the world’s first luxury paper.
它被用于制作乐器，作为捕鱼的绳索，甚至作为世界上首份奢侈品。
Eventually even the common people were able to wear garments of silk.
即使是普通人最终也能穿丝绸衣服

paragraphs.brief: 在汉王朝期间(206 BC-220 AD)，丝绸不再仅仅是织物，而成为一种货币形式。
sentences: During the Han dynasty (206 BC-220 AD), silk ceased to be a mere fabric and became a form of currency.
在汉王朝期间(206 BC-220 AD)，丝绸不再仅仅是织物，而成为一种货币形式。
Farmers paid their taxes in grain and silk, and silk was used to pay civil servants and to reward subjects for outstanding services.
农民缴纳谷物和丝绸税，用丝绸支付公务员和奖励优秀服务对象。
Values were calculated in lengths of silk as they had previously been calculated in weight of gold.
价值按丝长计算，而以前是按黄金重量计算。
Before long, silk became a currency used in trade with foreign countries, which continued into the Tang dynasty (616- 907 AD).
不久，丝绸成为与外国贸易中使用的一种货币，这种货币继续进入唐朝(616-907 AD)。
It is possible that this added importance was the result of a major increase in production.
增加的重要性可能是生产大幅度增加的结果。
Silk also found its way so thoroughly into the Chinese language that 230 of the 5,000 most common characters of Mandarin have ‘silk’ as their key component.
丝甚至深深融入了汉语：最常见的 5,000 个汉字中，有 230 个以“丝”为主要构字部件。

paragraphs.brief: 丝绸从早起就成为宝贵的商品，其他国家一直大力追求。人们相信，丝绸贸易实际上在不列颠哥伦比亚第二世纪正式开放之前就已经存在。
sentences: Silk became a precious commodity, highly sought after by other countries from an early date, and it is believed that the silk trade actually existed before the Silk Road was officially opened in the second century BC.
丝绸从早起就成为宝贵的商品，其他国家一直大力追求。人们相信，丝绸贸易实际上在不列颠哥伦比亚第二世纪正式开放之前就已经存在。

An Egyptian mummy with a silk thread in her hair, dating from 1070 BC, has been discovered in the village of Deir el Medina near the Valley of the Kings, and is probably the earliest evidence of the silk trade.
在帝王谷附近的代尔麦地那村，人们发现了一具头发中夹有丝线的埃及木乃伊，年代约为公元前 1070 年。这可能是迄今最早的丝绸贸易证据。
During the second century BC, the Chinese emperor Han Wu Di’s ambassadors travelled as far west as Persia and Mesopotamia, bearing gifts including silks.
在公元前二世纪，中国皇帝韩武迪的大使们远道西行，前往波斯和美索不达米亚，带了包括丝绸在内的礼物。
A range of important finds of Chinese silks have also been made along the Silk Road.
沿着丝绸之路也发现了一系列重要的中国丝绸
One of the most dramatic of these finds was some Tang silk discovered in 1900.
其中最戏剧性的发现之一是 1900年发现的唐丝绸。

It is believed that around 1015 AD Buddhist monks, possibly alarmed by the threat of invasion by Tibetan people, had sealed more than ten thousand manuscripts and silk paintings, silk banners and textiles in caves near Dunhuang, a trading station on the Silk Road in north-west China.
据信在公元1015年左右的佛教僧侣，可能担心西藏人可能会入侵他们，在西北中国丝之路的贸易站杜努安附近的洞穴里封闭了超过万份手稿和丝画，丝旗和织品。

paragraphs.brief: 罗马皇帝赫利奥加巴勒斯(218-222 AD)只穿丝绸。
sentences: Some historians believe the first Europeans to set eyes upon the fabulous fabric were the Roman legions of Marcus Licinius Crassus, Governor of Syria.
一些历史学家认为，第一批欧洲人看到这些神奇的布料，是叙利亚州长马库斯·利西纽斯·克拉萨斯的罗马军团。

According to certain accounts of the period, at an important battle near the Euphrates River in 53 BC, the Roman soldiers were so startled by the bright silken banners of the enemy that they fled in panic.
根据这一期间的某些说法，在公元前53年幼发拉底河附近发生的一场重要战斗中，罗马士兵被敌人的明亮丝绸旗帜惊吓，惊慌失措。
Yet, within decades Chinese silks were widely worn by the rich and noble families of Rome.
然而，在几十年内，罗马富人和高贵的家族广泛佩戴中国丝绸。
The Roman Emperor Heliogabalus (218-222 AD) wore nothing but silk.
罗马皇帝赫利奥加巴勒斯(218-222 AD)只穿丝绸。
By 380 AD, the Roman historian Ammianus Marcellinus reported that the use of silk, which was once confined to the nobility, had now spread to all classes without distinction—even to the lowest.
罗马历史学家Ammianus Marcellinus在380AD中报告说，曾经局限于贵族的丝绸的使用现在已经毫无区别地扩展到所有阶层，甚至扩大到最低阶层。
The desire for silk continued to increase over the centuries.
几百年来，对丝绸的渴望不断增长。
Despite this demand, the price of silk remained very high.
尽管有此要求，丝绸价格仍然很高。

paragraphs.brief: 尽管中国对生产方法保密，但中国最终失去了对丝绸生产的垄断权。
sentences: In spite of their secrecy about production methods, the Chinese eventually lost their monopoly on silk production.
尽管中国对生产方法保密，但中国最终失去了对丝绸生产的垄断权。
Knowledge of silk production methods reached Korea around 200 BC, when waves of Chinese immigrants arrived there.
中国移民潮抵达韩国时，朝鲜对丝绸生产方法的了解达到公元前200年左右。
Shortly after 300 AD, it travelled westward, and the cultivation of the silkworm was established in India.
300AD之后不久，它向西行进，在印度种植了丝虫。

paragraphs.brief: 大约550个AD丝质产品进入中东。
sentences: Around 550 AD silk production reached the Middle East.
大约550个AD丝质产品进入中东。

Records indicate that two monks from Constantinople (modern-day Istanbul), capital of the Byzantine Empire, appeared at their emperor’s court with silkworm eggs which they had obtained secretly, and hidden in their hollow bamboo walking sticks.
记录显示，来自拜占庭帝国首府君士坦丁堡(现代伊斯坦布尔)的两名僧侣带着他们秘密获取的丝虫蛋来到皇宫，藏在他们的空竹子中。
Under their supervision the eggs hatched into worms, and the worms spun silk threads.
在他们的监视下，卵子孵化成蠕虫，而蠕虫则刺穿丝线。
Byzantium was in the silk business at last.
拜占庭终于在做丝绸生意了
The Byzantine church and state created imperial workshops, monopolising production and keeping the secret to themselves.
拜占庭教会和邦创建了帝国工厂，垄断生产，并秘密进行。
This allowed a silk industry to be established, undercutting the market for ordinary-grade Chinese silk.
这使丝绸业得以建立，削弱了普通级中国丝绸市场。
However, high quality silk textiles, woven in China especially for the Middle Eastern market, continued to achieve high prices in the West, and trade along the Silk Road continued as before.
然而，中国的优质丝质纺织品，特别是在中东市场上的纺织，继续在西方实现高价格，丝绸之路沿线的贸易一如既往。
By the sixth century the Persians, too, had mastered the art of silk weaving, developing their own rich patterns and techniques.
到六世纪，波斯人也掌握了丝绸编织的艺术，发展了自己的丰富模式和技术。
But it wasn’t until the 13th century that Italy began silk production, with the introduction of 2,000 skilled silk weavers from Constantinople.
但直到13世纪，意大利才开始生产丝绸，引进了来自君士坦丁堡的2000个熟练的丝织品。
Eventually, silk production became widespread throughout Europe.
最终，丝绸生产在欧洲各地广泛推广。

paragraphs.brief: 在过去30年中，尽管人造纤维取代了丝绸的某些用途，但世界丝绸产量却增加了大约一倍。
sentences: World silk production has approximately doubled during the last 30 years in spite of manmade fibres replacing certain uses of silk.
在过去30年中，尽管人造纤维取代了丝绸的某些用途，但世界丝绸产量却增加了大约一倍。
Before this period, China and Japan were the two main producers, together manufacturing more than 50 per cent of world production each year.
在此之前，中国和日本是两个主要生产国，它们每年生产的世界产量超过50%。
After the late 1970s, however, China dramatically increased its silk production, and once again became the world’s leading producer.
然而，在1970年代后期之后，中国的丝绸生产急剧增加，再次成为世界主要生产国。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

items.en: Their first sight of silk created fear among Roman soldiers.
items.zh: 他们第一次看到丝绸使罗马士兵产生恐惧
items.why: 罗马士兵被敌军鲜亮的丝质旗帜吓得惊慌逃跑，符合“见到丝绸后恐惧”。

items.en: The quality of Chinese silk imported by the early Romans varied widely.
items.zh: 早期罗马人进口的中国丝绸的质量差别很大。
items.why: 文章说中国丝绸后来流行于罗马富裕家庭，并没有比较进口丝绸的质量差异。

items.en: The Byzantine emperor first acquired silkworm eggs from the Chinese emperor.
items.zh: 拜占庭皇帝先从中国皇帝那里获得丝虫蛋
items.why: 题干称“和拜占庭皇帝从中国皇帝那里得到乔卵"。原文强调“僧侣秘密获取并偷运到君士坦丁堡”,并非来自中国皇帝的正式获取，故与题干矛盾,FALSE。

items.en: The price of high-grade Chinese silk fell due to competition from Middle-Eastern producers.
items.zh: 中国高档丝绸的价格由于中东生产商的竞争而下降。
items.why: 题干称“高档中国丝绸因中东生产者的竞争而降价"。原文相反: 虽然拜占庭等地建立毕业、压低了普通中国丝，但高质量中国丝在西方仍保持高价，故 FALSE。

items.en: Silk was produced in the Middle East several centuries before it was produced in Europe.
items.zh: 丝绸是在中东生产，在欧洲生产前几个世纪。
items.why: 中东 (拜占庭/波斯) 在6世纪已会产丝。欧洲 (意大利) 要到13 世纪才开始，时间差“several centuries”。与题干一致,TRUE。

items.en: Global silk production has declined in recent years.
items.zh: 近年来，全球丝绸产量有所下降。
items.why: 题干称“全球丝绸产量下降”。原文明确“近 30 年翻倍",且中国在70年代末后“大幅增加”,与题干相反,FALSE。

pairs: 题干用动词，定位句改用同词根的名词。
第 2 段 · 第 2 句
第 4 段 · 第 6 句
第 8 段 · 第 1 句
points: 题干称“全球丝绸产量下降”。原文明确“近 30 年翻倍",且中国在70年代末后“大幅增加”,与题干相反,FALSE。
回到对应内容“在帝王谷附近的代尔麦地那村，人们发现了一具头发中夹有丝线的埃及木乃伊，年代约为公元前 1070 年。这可能是迄今最早的丝绸贸易证据”，再按题干要求写出答案。
clauses: Silk also found its way so thoroughly into the Chinese language ….
“that 230 of the 5,000 most common characters of Mandarin have ‘silk’ as their key component”补足 found 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 found 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
Before long, silk became a currency used in trade with foreign countries, … ).
“which continued into the Tang dynasty (616- 907 AD”修饰前面的 countries。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 which 时，回看 countries，再把修饰信息接回主句。
lead: Silk, a natural fibre produced by a particular worm called a silkworm, has been used in clothing for many centuries.
丝绸是一种天然纤维，由一种叫作丝虫的虫子生产，许多世纪以来一直用于衣着。
